newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on NOPA, soybean break.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on NOPA, soybean break.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended lower in reaction to Friday's National Oilseed Processors Association data which suggested to some market watchers that stocks were not as tight as previously believed, traders said.
"The amount of beans in the crushers' hands was abundant," said John Kleist, director of agricultural research for ING Futures and Options in Chicago.

NOPA on Friday put soybean ownership in all positions at roughly 136 million bushels, surprising some who had anticipated a lower figure. NOPA also said exports during May totaled 288,456 tons, below April's tally of 416,109 tons.
Floor sources noted the report suggested ample supplies, yet processors continued to crush at a rapid pace as evidenced by the weekly NOPA crush reports.

Cash sources pointed to strong crush margins and anticipation of a decline in margins later this month. They cited expectations for a jump in soybean prices as shorts liquidated the July ahead of first notice day.
Soymeal ended $5.40 to $4.00 per ton lower with July off $4.70 at $276.40. Soyoil closed 0.27 to 0.15 cent per lb lower with July down 0.20 at 23.13.
Soy products were also hit by a late slide in soybeans.
Soybeans collapsed in late trade on heavy outright selling in the July and on profit taking on the July/November spread, pit sources said.

Weather also drew bearish reviews. Forecasts called for showers across much of the U.S. Midwest, followed by warming temperatures, meteorologists said. Floor traders said that combination would be ideal for crop development.

On the day, volume was said to be thin in both soymeal and soyoil. In meal, Cargill Inc bought 200 July and sold 100 December, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 200 July and sold 100 July, and Merrill Lynch sold 200 July. Central Soya spread 150 lots December/March at $6.00 per ton, premium December.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 100 lots each July and September and sold 100 July. Iowa Grain bought 100 July and sold 100 December, and Refco Inc sold 100 July.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 24,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 34,845 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 10,000 lots, against Friday's 11,919.
